[[Captain/Legends|Captain]] '''Trask Lucan''' was a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Reproduction/Legends|born]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Hyder]]. The son of a [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]], Lucan became a [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] [[Agent/Legends|agent]] and [[Scout/Legends|scout]] during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. On the planet [[Glova]], he was set up by the local [[Governor/Legends|governor]] [[Tegist Byrg]] and lost his [[Starship/Legends|ship]], the ''[[Lucan's Nightmare]]''. Unable to leave the planet, he stayed on Glova until he met a group of [[Smuggler/Legends|smugglers]] who were in a similar situation. With the aid of the New Republic [[Ambassador/Legends|ambassador]] [[Robet Makina]], they attacked Byrg's headquarters in order to retrieve their ships.

==Biography==
Trask Lucan was [[Reproduction/Legends|born]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Hyder]]. His [[Trask Lucan's father|father]] had been a [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]], and Lucan inherited his piloting skills. He flew his first solo flight at a very young age, and from that time onward he was always at the controls of a [[Starship/Legends|starship]]. When his father was shot down by the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] after being suspected of [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggling]], Lucan swore vengeance.<ref name="TPOC" />

At some point in his life, Lucan became a [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] [[Agent/Legends|agent]] and obtained a ship and named it the ''[[Lucan's Nightmare]]''. Acting as an advance [[Scout/Legends|scout]] for the New Republic, he arrived on the neutral planet [[Glova]], where he was set up by the planetary [[Governor/Legends|governor]] [[Tegist Byrg]], who had been secretly working for the Empire and who confiscated his ship. Stranded on the planet, and with only his [[Heavy blaster pistol/Legends|heavy blaster pistol]] and [[Environment suit/Legends|vacuum suit]] left, Lucan kept his connections with the New Republic secret and was often found in the local [[Cantina/Legends|cantinas]] posing as a mere tramp [[Freighter/Legends|freighter]] pilot. In [[Borke's Cantina]], he met a group of smugglers while they were looking for a way to get their ship out of the impound. Lucan later assisted them along with [[Soldier/Legends|soldiers]] under the command of New Republic [[Ambassador/Legends|ambassador]] [[Robet Makina]] in a raid on Byrg's headquarters to reclaim their ships after it was revealed that the governor had connections with the Empire.<ref name="TPOC" />

==Personality and traits==
Trask Lucan stood 1.7 [[Meter/Legends|meters]] tall and was a strong, agile man with an athletic build, [[Color/Legends|brown]] [[Hair/Legends|hair]] in a shaggy mop, and gray [[Eye/Legends|eyes]]. He usually dressed as a tramp freighter pilot. He was a gifted pilot, a skilled [[Technician/Legends|mechanic]], and a knowledgeable person. He was especially fluent in [[astrography]] and the structure of [[Realspace/Legends|space]] freighters. Lucan knew how to talk to people and sometimes was seen [[Gambling/Legends|gambling]].<ref name="TPOC" />

Trask was known for his optimism. He had a talent for acting, one that allowed him to play the part of a downtrodden ship captain, while in truth he was always quite happy with the way things had gone. Lucan was very brash and felt a strong enthusiasm for the New Republic, an enthusiasm matched only by his keenness for [[Alcohol/Legends|strong drink]].<ref name="TPOC" />

==Behind the scenes==
Lucan's first and only appearance in the ''[[Star Wars Legends]]'' continuity is in ''[[The Politics of Contraband]]'', an adventure for ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]'' written by [[Bill Smith]], published by [[West End Games]] in [[1991]], and anthologized in [[Classic Adventures|''Classic Adventures: Volume 1'']]. He serves as a non-player character who assists a party of players on their quest to reclaim their ship by capturing the planetary governor and who tries to get his own ship back as well. Since Tegist Byrg can either be captured or escape on Lucan's ship at the end of the adventure, Lucan can either get the ''Lucan's Nightmare'' back or let the players try to do so by following the governor. In the second option, however, the fate of the ''Nightmare'' remains uncertain, since the adventure ends as the players set off to find Byrg.<ref name="TPOC" />
